transcript: This play was 10/10 rage bait but in a good way. Bull by Mike Bartlett is a searing one-act about three corporate employees gearing up for a layoff, knowing only two of them will make it past the cut. The characters are so insanely terrible to one another, and with times being as tough as they are, they do not hold back from backstabbing and throwing each other under the bus at any chance they get. I thought the acting was really good and that these characters were super believable, which made it easy to dislike them. And this was the rage bait part — having to sit in a small room as a fly on the wall while they said and did some truly despicable things. But the performances are also quite funny at times, and there's some comedic relief in how unhinged it is. That said, the overall premise of the situation is realistic and it feels allegorical. There's a clear cynicism baked into the play in what it says about human nature and our capitalistic, dog-eat-dog world, and I really liked that aspect of it. It's not everyday you see something that's hard to enjoy but is nevertheless something you like and appreciate. For me, this was one of those pieces. With that, another program for my collection.
